knowledge_point.title: Identifying Equilibrium Solutions of a Differential Equation

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{y^{2} - 1}{y^{2}}.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y\ne0$.

We need

$$
f(c)=\frac{c^{2} - 1}{c^{2}}=0.
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=\frac{\left(2\right)^{2} - 1}{\left(2\right)^{2}} \\ &=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=\frac{\left(1\right)^{2} - 1}{\left(1\right)^{2}} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=\frac{\left(-1\right)^{2} - 1}{\left(-1\right)^{2}} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=1$ and $y=-1$.

\frac{dy}{dt} = - y^{2} - 3 y - 2.
$$

We need

$$
f(c)=- c^{2} - 3 c - 2=0.
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- \left(2\right)^{2} - 3 \left(2\right) - 2 \\ &=-12\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=- \left(-1\right)^{2} - 3 \left(-1\right) - 2 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=- \left(-2\right)^{2} - 3 \left(-2\right) - 2 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-1$ and $y=-2$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = - y - \sin{\left(y \right)} - \pi.
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

We need

$$
f(c)=- c - \sin{\left(c \right)} - \pi=0.
$$

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=- \pi + 0 - \sin{\left(0 \right)} \\ &=- \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=- \pi$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(- \pi) &=- \pi - \sin{\left(- \pi \right)} + \pi \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=\pi$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\pi) &=- \pi - \pi - \sin{\left(\pi \right)} \\ &=- 2 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=- \pi$.

$$

question.:question/worked-solution:

First keep the original domain: $y>0$.

We need

$$
f(c)=c^{2} \ln{\left(c \right)} - e^{2}=0.
$$

- For $c=e$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(e) &=- e^{2} + e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- e^{2} + 4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=- e^{2} + 1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ &=- e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e$.

First keep the original domain: $y + 1>0$.

$$
f(c)=\left(c + 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c + 1 \right)}=0.

$$

- For $c=0$:
